items.prompt: A GB worker's active employment has salaryAmountMinor 650000 and employerCostRateBps 1600. PayrollService.create runs for her organization and country. What EMPLOYER_COST item amount is created?
distractors: 10400 minor units, which is GBP 104.00
1040000 minor units, which is GBP 10,400.00
650000 minor units, the same as base pay
items.explanation: The item is Math.round(salary * bps / 10000) = 650000 * 1600 / 10000 = 104000. Basis points are hundredths of a percent, so 1600 bps is 16%.

items.prompt: A worker earns salaryAmountMinor 440000. She has one APPROVED UNPAID time-off request of 3 days overlapping the period, and one REQUESTED unpaid request of 2 days. What DEDUCTION item does create add for her?
items.answer: -60000, for 3 approved days at salary / 22 each
distractors: -100000, for all 5 days across both of the requests
-40000, as 3 of a 33-day month are deducted
No deduction until the cycle reaches APPROVED
items.explanation: Only UNPAID requests with status APPROVED that overlap the period count, so 3 days. The deduction is -Math.round(440000 / 22 * 3) = -60000, using an assumed 22 working days a month.

items.prompt: A GBP-paid worker has two expenses in status APPROVED_FOR_PAYROLL with no payroll cycle: one of GBP 120.00 and one of EUR 80.00. A new payroll cycle is created. What happens to them?
items.answer: Only the GBP one becomes a reimbursement item
distractors: Both are reimbursed, the EUR one converted to GBP at a stored rate
Neither is touched: expenses are only attached through attach-payroll
The create call fails, since it cannot add money across currencies
items.explanation: create loads approved, unattached expenses filtered by currency equal to the employment's salary currency. Only the GBP one matches, becomes an EXPENSE_REIMBURSEMENT item and gets the cycle id; the EUR expense is left for later.

items.prompt: An APPROVED payroll cycle has three GBP items: BASE_PAY 500000, EMPLOYER_COST 70000 and a DEDUCTION of -20000. What totalMinor does createFromPayroll put on the invoice?
items.explanation: The subtotal sums every item, including the negative deduction: 550000. The service fee is Math.round(550000 * 0.07) = 38500, and the total is 588500.

items.prompt: Operations calls createFromPayroll on a cycle that is still in CLIENT_REVIEW and has no invoice yet. What happens?
items.answer: A 400, since payroll must be approved before invoicing
distractors: An invoice is created, as review is the last stage before approval
A 400, because the cycle already has an invoice attached to it
An invoice is created in DRAFT, to be issued after approval
items.explanation: createFromPayroll accepts only APPROVED, LOCKED, PROCESSED or CLOSED cycles. CLIENT_REVIEW is not in that list, so it throws "Payroll must be approved before an invoice can be generated."

items.prompt: A payroll cycle is APPROVED. An operator calls advance with nextStatus CLOSED to finish the period in one step. What does assertTransition do?
items.answer: It throws; APPROVED may only move to LOCKED
distractors: Allows it, since CLOSED is a terminal state
Allows it, as editability is checked instead
Throws, because closed cycles need an invoice
items.explanation: payrollCycleTransitions lists APPROVED: ["LOCKED"]. Anything else, CLOSED included, fails assertTransition with "Invalid status transition from APPROVED to CLOSED."; the cycle must go LOCKED, then PROCESSED, then CLOSED.

items.prompt: An approved organization creates a hire request for a GB worker with salaryCurrency USD. What does HiringService.create do?
items.answer: It is refused, since GB salaries must be in GBP
distractors: Creates it and converts the salary into GBP
Creates it, since currency is only checked later
Refuses it: only US workers may be paid in USD
items.explanation: create loads the country profile and throws when country.defaultCurrency differs from dto.salaryCurrency. GB's default is GBP, so the message is "Salary currency for GB must be GBP."

items.prompt: A hire request is SUBMITTED; it never went through INTERNAL_REVIEW or READY_FOR_WORKER. Ops calls approveForWorker. What happens?
items.answer: It succeeds, and the request jumps straight to WORKER_ONBOARDING
distractors: It fails, since the state machine needs READY_FOR_WORKER first
It fails, because approval is only possible from INTERNAL_REVIEW
It succeeds, but the request is moved to READY_FOR_WORKER only
items.explanation: approveForWorker uses an inline check that allows SUBMITTED or INTERNAL_REVIEW, not assertTransition. It then sets WORKER_ONBOARDING, skipping states the transition map would require (the walkthrough flags this as a refactor).

items.prompt: A worker's vacation balance for the year has allowanceDays 15 and usedDays 13. A manager approves her REQUESTED 3-day VACATION request. What does review return?
items.answer: A 400, as approving would exceed the vacation balance
distractors: It is approved, and usedDays is capped at the 15-day allowance
It is approved, leaving usedDays at 16 for the year
A 400, since only 2 days could ever be requested
items.explanation: review computes usedAfter = 13 + 3 = 16 and throws when that exceeds allowanceDays 15, before the transaction that would update the request and increment usedDays.

items.prompt: addMoney is called with [money(10000, "GBP"), money(25000, "GBP"), money(5000, "USD")]. What is the result?
items.answer: It throws, since adding across currencies needs FX
distractors: 40000 GBP, with the USD item treated as GBP
35000 GBP, as the USD item is skipped silently
40000 in USD, since the last item currency sets the total
items.explanation: The reducer compares each remaining item with the first one's currency and throws "Cannot add money across currencies without an FX conversion." on the USD item.

items.prompt: A worker submits a time-off request from Monday to Friday of the same week with days: 1. What does TimeOffService.create store?
items.answer: A request recording 1 day, exactly as sent
distractors: A request for 5 days, computed from the dates
A 400, as the days do not match the dates
A request for 7 days, counting the weekend
items.explanation: create only checks that endDate is not before startDate and stores dto.days as given. The DTO requires at least 0.5, but nothing compares days with the date range.

items.prompt: A payroll cycle is APPROVED but not yet LOCKED. Someone approves a bonus adjustment that targets it, so assertEditable is called. What does it do?
items.answer: It passes, as only LOCKED, PROCESSED and CLOSED are protected
distractors: Throws, since an approved cycle may no longer be changed at all
Throws, because adjustments can only target OPEN payroll cycles
Lets it through, then moves the cycle back to INTERNAL_REVIEW
items.explanation: isPayrollCycleEditable returns false only for LOCKED, PROCESSED and CLOSED. APPROVED is editable, so the adjustment item can still be added after client approval.

items.front: Why can two concurrent vacation approvals overdraw a balance?
items.back: review checks usedDays + days against allowanceDays BEFORE opening the transaction that increments usedDays. Two approvals can both read the old usedDays and both pass. Fix: check inside the transaction, or a conditional update (usedDays + days <= allowanceDays) that checks the affected row count.

items.front: Why are payroll adjustments a separate model from payroll items?
items.back: An adjustment is the business event with its own approval workflow (who asked, why, who approved). The payroll item is its calculated inclusion in one pay run. Keeping both preserves the reason behind every line on the payroll.

items.front: How do the domain state machines work in packages/domain/src/states.ts?
items.back: Each is an object mapping a status to the statuses it may move to, declared as const so the status type is derived from its keys. assertTransition(map, from, to) throws "Invalid status transition" when to is not listed; terminal states have empty arrays.

items.front: What is the design lesson of feature 34 (expenses into payroll)?
items.back: Approval and inclusion are separate. An expense can be APPROVED_FOR_PAYROLL long before a specific payroll run picks it up, and inclusion must respect the run being editable. Linking the expense and creating the item happen in one transaction.
